outcome: Predictive value of D-dimer for venous thromboembolism (VTE)
cohort: 240 pregnant women seeking routine perinatal care and delivery at a hospital between January 2018 and January 2019
finding: D-dimer levels increase throughout pregnancy and are higher in pregnant women compared to non-pregnant women, with the second-trimester D-dimer level demonstrating the highest predictive value for VTE.
mod_finding: D-dimer levels were higher in pregnant women who had cesarean sections compared to those who had vaginal deliveries.
